codex-rs/codex-mcp/src/connection_manage.basis: additional source inspected directly; frozen baseline unchanged

observed_behavior: Actual stdio process, Streamable HTTP session and host-supported SSE connection are reused within their owner, including after synchronous discovery bridge runtimes end. Concurrent initialization is serialized without duplicating processes.

Source/configuration or resolved credential changes invalidate the connection key; secrets are hashed and not stored in the key or diagnostics. Package cwd/header source validation runs before each reuse.

Startup timeout includes initialization and initial tools/list; call timeout, dropped futures, request cancellation, process exit, disabled configuration and plugin disable close the owned connection. Unix tests wait for actual child process exit/reaping.
Native ownership uses tenant/workspace/session keys and is released on archive/delete. ACP SessionToolset owns a separate cloneable lease; retained tool bindings cannot keep an ended lease usable.

Validated positive lifecycle timeouts, required and connection/catalog readiness declarations are retained in host metadata. Only the local execution environment is admitted. Actual required startup failure blocks common tool execution.
Legacy array and map packages both receive host-owned source context, enabling source-specific disable cleanup. The original package and all runtime marker/state locations stay separate.
intentional_safety_differences: Legacy protocols remain private per chat; cross-chat MCP 2026-07-28 negotiation and account/auth-generation sharing are not impersonated.
Lifecycle timeouts must be positive with at least millisecond resolution. A cancelled/timed-out call retires the client rather than reusing a connection with uncertain outstanding server work.
The existing serialized per-connection request path prioritizes ownership/cancellation safety; no claim of parallel remote calls or subscription support.
